structural: The structural obligations in `requirements.sdk.outlines.parser` are the `OutlineContent` type with private fields, the listed constructors and accessors with their signatures, the `Clone`, `Debug` and `NodeContents` implementations, and the delegation rule that `from_id` uses the same cached file as `from_path` and then selects the item. Each one has a root with an {impl} marker, and the source matches it.

- **Type and Clone:** `struct[OutlineContent]` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs` has only private fields (`id`, `snapshot: Arc<Snapshot>`, `selected`) and derives `Clone`. This meets the "private fields" and `impl Clone` clauses.
- **Constructors and accessors:** `impl[OutlineContent]` declares `from_path`, `from_id`, `from_source`, `from_path_with`, `from_source_with`, `select`, `id`, `text`, `source_span`, `source_span_redacted`, `outline`, `language`, `structural_hash` and `fingerprint_scheme`. I read the headers of `from_path`, `from_id` and `from_source`, and the outline listing shows the other headers. All of them match the prescribed signatures. I did not read the bodies of `from_path_with`, `from_source_with` or the accessors, because the clauses I checked there constrain only signatures.
- **Cache use and delegation:** `from_path` reads and fills `cache.outlines`, so it uses the supplied validation cache. `from_id` is `Self::from_path(cache, &id.path)?.select(&id.selector)`. That is the "same cached file, then select the addressed item" delegation the text prescribes. An alternative that re-read the file in `from_id` would break this clause, so the clause is structural. This implementation honors it.
- **Language inference:** `from_path` and `from_source` go through `parse_source`. It uses `languages::registry().for_path` and falls back to `PlainText`. The text only cites `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults` for the language mappings and does not prescribe them here, so they need no evidence under this requirement.
- **Trait implementations:** `impl[OutlineContent/std::fmt::Debug]` and `impl[OutlineContent/NodeContents]` provide the `Debug` and `NodeContents` implementations.

The four supplied roots carry the {impl} marker, and I found no unmarked root or unreached structural obligation.

behavioral: The subject states these behavioral obligations: `OutlineContent::from_path` returns root contents using the supplied validation cache. `from_id` uses the same cached file and selects the addressed item. Both infer the language from the filename under `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`. The signature listing is covered by the public API export test. The text states no separate behavior for `from_source`, `from_path_with`, `from_source_with` or the accessors beyond what they do here.

Coverage by test:
- **`from_path` returns root contents.**
  - `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[file_constructors_infer_the_language_and_return_addressed_contents]` asserts the root selector is `""`, the text equals the whole source, and the item selectors are `["", "fn[check_token]"]`.
  - `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits]` asserts root text for a plain-text file.
  - `tests/contracts.rs#fn[domain_clones_share_the_first_successful_outline_for_each_path]` asserts the root has an empty selector and the original text.
- **`from_path` uses the supplied cache.**
  - In `domain_clones_share_the_first_successful_outline_for_each_path`, a first `from_path` on a missing file errors.
  - The next `from_path` on the same cache returns the snapshot of the original contents.
  - After the file is overwritten, `from_path` through a different cache (`Application::default().cache()`) returns the new contents.
  - `from_path` through the shared cache returns the same `Outline` object (`ptr::eq`) with the original text.
  - Other-path lookups through the domain clones share the cache even after the file is deleted.
  - A cache that returned nothing, or a global cache, would fail these assertions.
- **`from_id` uses the same cached file and selects the addressed item.**
  - In `domain_clones_share_the_first_successful_outline_for_each_path`, `from_id(peer.cache(), fn[first])` is called after the file was deleted and overwritten. It still yields `fn first() {}`, which shows the cached file is reused.
  - `file_constructors_infer_the_language_and_return_addressed_contents` checks `selected.id()`, `selected.text()` and that the fingerprint equals the one from `root.select`.
  - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` checks a plain-text line selected via `from_id`. It also checks that `from_id` on a fresh cache errors once the file has changed and the selector no longer exists.
- **Language inference from the filename under `defaults`.**
  - The uppercase `AUTH.RS` is treated as Rust (scheme `rust-structural-v1`, `fn[check_token]` item). This exercises case-insensitive matching for both `from_path` and `from_id`.
  - `notes.unknown` falls back to the plain-text outline (one child per nonblank line, 3 items including the root) for both `from_path` and `from_id`.
  - The per-language mappings belong to the cited `defaults` requirement and are not reassessed here.
- **Error cases.** Missing-file errors are asserted for `from_path` and for `from_id`.
- **Declared API shape.** `tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the exports against rustdoc.

I found no uncovered observable obligation.

pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
pub fn source_span(&self, span: Span) -> Option<&str>;
pub fn source_span_redacted(&self, span: Span) -> Option<Cow<'_, str>>;
The filename-based constructors include Rust, Python, TypeScript, TSX,
Markdown, CSS, TOML, and YAML languages. Extension matching is
case-insensitive, using each implementation's claimed extensions.
A filename without a claimed extension uses the
